cut_items.item: Explicitly says not to delete anything else in /var/lib/postgresql except via PostgreSQL commands

Suggests finding the root cause of log growth (log_statement='all', error loops)
Names long-running transactions as a possible cause of WAL retention
Gives an actual SQL query to list largest tables
Notes that a replica that is merely down should be restarted, and that a dropped slot means the replica cannot resume
Says that wrong WAL deletion can break replicas and recovery, not just corrupt the database
Verification target: usage below 80% rather than just under 90%

Escalation if PostgreSQL has stopped or if unsure whether a slot can be dropped

Check pg_stat_archiver failed_count growing as the sign that archiving is failing
Check for a long-running transaction as a cause of retained WAL

added_items.item: Warns against moving or editing pg_wal files, not only deleting them

Copy logs elsewhere before removing them if needed for audits
Check that log rotation is running and fix it if it is not

Dropping a slot may force the consumer to do a full resync

Remove data only after the owning team confirms it is not needed

Recheck after 10 minutes that pg_wal is not growing
Confirm the alert clears and record the cause in incident notes
